senses.definition: A person who is recognized by a university as having completed the requirements of a degree studied at the institution.
examples: If the government wants graduates to stay in the country they should offer more incentives.

senses.definition: (US, Canada) A person who is recognized by a high school as having completed the requirements of a course of study at the school.
(Philippines) A person who is recognized as having completed any level of education.
A graduated (marked) cup or other container, thus fit for measuring.
(intransitive, ergative) To be recognized by a school or university as having completed the requirements of a degree studied at the institution.

quotes.text: After graduating from Princeton University, he earned a law degree in Canada, then worked as an environmental lawyer in Israel before settling on the south side of Youngstown.
quotes.reference: 2019 February 19, Jeremy Pelzer, “Youngstown School Board member Dario Hunter seeks Green Party presidential nomination”, in cleveland.com:

senses.definition: (transitive, proscribed) To be certified as having earned a degree from; to graduate from (an institution).
(transitive) To certify (a student) as having earned a degree
examples: The college graduated him as soon as he was no longer eligible to play under NCAA rules.

senses.definition: (transitive) To mark (something) with degrees; to divide into regular steps or intervals, as the scale of a thermometer, a scheme of punishment or rewards, etc.

examples: sandstone which graduates into gneiss; carnelian sometimes graduates into quartz

quotes.text: As the species graduate into each other, both in form and in habits, from the grass-eating Geese to the fish-eating Harelds, it is difficult, […] to divide this large group into sections.
quotes.reference: 1852, William Macgillivray, A history of British birds, indigenous and migratory, page 573:

quotes.text: Yadav, born Bharat Kalicharan, was a petty thief who had graduated to bigger crimes, terrorising Kasturba Nagar, on the edge of the city of Nagpur, in Maharashtra, from the 1990s until his death.
quotes.reference: 2022 November 7, Puja Bhattacharjee, “What drove 200 women to stab a gangster to death? Netflix series revisits crime that shocked India”, in the Guardian:

senses.definition: To prepare gradually; to arrange, temper, or modify by degrees or to a certain degree; to determine the degrees of.
examples: to graduate the heat of an oven

quotes.text: Dyers, who advance and graduate their colours with salts.
quotes.reference: 1650, Thomas Browne, Pseudodoxia Epidemica: […], 2nd edition, London: […] A[braham] Miller, for Edw[ard] Dod and Nath[aniel] Ekins, […], →OCLC:

senses.definition: (chemistry) To bring to a certain degree of consistency, by evaporation, as a fluid.
(intransitive) To taper, as the tail of certain birds.
(transitive, software engineering) To approve (a feature) for general release.
examples: We have graduated the new machine-learning features and will roll them out tomorrow.

senses.definition: (intransitive, Japanese entertainment) Of an idol: to exit a group; or of a virtual YouTuber, to leave a management agency; usually accompanied with "graduation ceremony" send-offs, increased focus on the leaving member, and the like.
examples: Fans speculate that she was forced to graduate due to harassment and doxxing by stalkers and haters.
